items.summary: This repository provides three physics-based datasets for developing and evaluating surrogate models to identify the seismic failure modes (SFMs) of coastal reinforced concrete bridge bents supported by pile-group foundations under combined scour and corrosion. Each sample contains 20 input variables: 17 structural and geotechnical parameters, scour depth, and the corrosion levels of longitudinal and transverse column reinforcement. The output is one of three SFMs: column flexural failure (CFF), foundation flexural failure (FFF), or column shear-associated failure (CSF). These labels are determined through nonlinear finite element analysis and code-based shear capacity calculations. The datasets support reproducible surrogate model development and subsequent life-cycle probabilistic assessment of SFMs and their transitions in deteriorating coastal bridge bents.

items.summary: We examine the role of the compact Lie group $SO(3)\times O(2)$ in the metric critical-point theory of normalized thick knots. The quotient by this group is part of the construction of ropelength-filtered knot spaces, but passage to an orbit space need not preserve the weak-slope notion of criticality. We establish elementary structural results for the action, including finiteness of isotropy for nontrivial knot types and exact invariance of the descending strong slope under a compact isometric quotient. We give counterexamples, including one with the connected group $SO(2)$, showing that the analogous assertion for the weak slope fails in general. On the other hand, we prove that it does hold, up to a multiplicative constant, at every point where the orbit map admits a Lipschitz local section together with a continuous gauge, and we construct such data for normalized thick knots from finitely many Fourier modes. Consequently, on the open stratum of thick knots with trivial isotropy, weak-slope criticality on the parametrized model and on the quotient coincide; at a configuration with nontrivial finite isotropy $\Gamma$ we show that finitely many Fourier modes recover $\Gamma$ exactly, and that the comparison problem is equivalent, up to constants, to the same problem for the finite group $\Gamma$ acting on a slice. items.summary: Cardiorenal syndrome (CRS) is a complex condition involving bidirectional interactions between cardiovascular and renal dysfunction. Its pathophysiology includes hemodynamic abnormalities, venous congestion, neurohormonal activation, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and metabolic disturbances. This narrative review aims to analyze the mechanisms of CRS and assess the relationship between renal function and clinical prognosis in patients with cardiovascular diseases, focusing on mortality, heart failure hospitalization, kidney dysfunction progression, and treatment-related renal changes. The review synthesizes evidence from clinical guidelines, randomized trials, observational studies, and contemporary scientific publications, with particular attention to CRS classification, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), serum creatinine, albuminuria, biomarkers, and treatment outcomes. The evidence indicates that reduced eGFR, albuminuria, persistent congestion, and worsening renal function provide complementary prognostic information. An analysis of 3,715 EVEREST trial participants found that each 30% decline in eGFR was associated with an increased risk of death and cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. The DOSE trial showed that intensive diuretic treatment could improve fluid removal and symptoms while increasing short-term creatinine elevations. These findings highlight the importance of interpreting renal function changes alongside congestion, hemodynamic stability, baseline kidney function, and treatment response. Comprehensive cardiorenal risk assessment should incorporate renal function, albuminuria, urine output, cardiac biomarkers, electrolyte status, and clinical response to treatment. Further prospective studies are needed to validate integrated risk models in diverse patient populations.

items.summary: Unrefereed research candidate. A wide binary star takes thousands of years to complete one orbit, so its eccentricity usually cannot be found by following the orbit. Astronomers instead use the angle Γ between the pair's projected separation and projected relative velocity, whose distribution over many binaries depends on the population's eccentricity law. Hwang, Ting and Zakamska (MNRAS 2022, Appendix B) asked whether this angle distribution determines the eccentricity distribution uniquely. In the ideal model (random orbital phase, uniformly random 3D orientation, error-free projections) this package derives the likelihood of one angle in closed form, p(γ|e) = [acosh(1/e) − 1{|cos γ| > e} acosh(|cos γ|/e)] / (π sin²γ), and shows that its mixtures are classical Abel transforms. This gives an explicit inverse for every eccentricity law, including atoms: different eccentricity laws never give the same angle law. The inverse is continuous in the weak topology but discontinuous in total variation, so fine structure can be nearly invisible. Moments need no inversion: E√(1−e²) = (π/2) E sin³Γ and E e² = 1/2 + E cos 2Γ − (1/2) E cos 4Γ; these are the only symmetric unbiased single-angle observables for their targets and give near-efficient power-law index estimators. Two exact selection results bear on Gaia samples: thermal populations keep a uniform angle law under selections that ignore sky position angles, and binning by projected separation preserves the model under a log-uniform semimajor-axis law. The archive contains the 21-page manuscript (PDF and LaTeX source) with complete proofs, a Python library (likelihoods, observables, estimators, Kepler simulators), the full validation script with recorded results and figures, semantic negative controls, fast CI checks, the bounded novelty report and SHA-256 sums. Its core three-coupling is AI modeling, formulation constraints, and external generalization. The central falsifiable test is not a favorable random-split score: a model frozen in advance must survive complete raw-material-lot holdouts and forward-in-time evaluation against strong, resource-matched conventional baselines. The study separates botanical species and chemotype authentication, formula mass-fraction closure, sample and instrument provenance, physicochemical endpoints, safety restrictions and predictive uncertainty. It tests whether nominal AI improvements are explained instead by duplicate aliquots, batch identifiers, chronological leakage, correlated chemistry, imbalance across rare botanical families or extra measurement budget. It preserves original outcome units and treats unsafe or unqualified ingredient combinations as hard exclusions rather than soft optimization penalties. Thirty distinct mathematical research plates cover external risk, compositional closure and log ratios, hierarchical lot variance, analytical censoring, physical rheology and diffusion, Gaussian-process predictions, constrained acquisition, Pareto comparisons, distribution shift, calibrated intervals, noncompensatory safety gates and evidence provenance. Eighty-two research chapters are followed by 410 individually paginated studies. Two hundred Research Gates pose prospective falsification questions, including blinded material substitution, negative controls, independent metrology, worst-supplier performance, safe abstention and external replay. Thirty-three different Phoenix Answer Embryos propose distinct testable instruments, protocols, audits and evidence artifacts for future investigators. items.summary: A phase-only spatial light modulator in the pupil of a microscope objective can form hundreds to thousands of optical traps at once, but only if the phase pattern it displays is computed well: the pattern fixes how much light reaches the traps, how equal the traps are, where stray light goes, how the pattern survives a real device, and how fast it can be recomputed when traps move. DinHot is an open studio that runs 24 methods (19 published ones and 5 proposed here) on the same task, with the same seeds, metrics and device model, in Python as the reference and in a TypeScript port that runs live in a browser. We describe the optical and device model, the methods with the measured acceptance of each, 14 cases from a 3 x 3 array to a disordered 819-trap array and shaped potentials, the benchmark protocol, two learned models, and the 5 proposed methods, three of which meet their acceptance criteria on their acceptance tasks, each within a scope that the benchmark or the scope measurements narrow (a device-aware weighted Gerchberg-Saxton update, a flicker-bounded phase-continuous sequence and an efficiency-uniformity front), one of which meets a narrowed criterion (an aberration-robust hologram) and one of which is refuted by measurement (a learned warm start for phase-fixed weighted GS). A network trained on three-plane volumes beats its baseline at equal wall-clock on all 162 held-out volumes (median accuracy ratio 1.140), whereas its two-dimensional counterpart ties with Gerchberg-Saxton (ratio 0.9994). The model is a scalar Fourier model of a simulated device, not a calibrated instrument. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . Interactive studio: https://dinhot.fasl-work.com .

items.summary: This dataset contains the supplementary material to the article “Adaptive Event Disambiguation via Alignments with Deferred Decisions” , submitted to the journal Process Science. datasets/ : the two synthetically generated datasets used in the evaluation, each in its own folder ( blood_donation , smart_home ). Each folder contains: runs.txt : the normative process behavior as a set of reference runs (one run per line), i.e. the model log against which traces are aligned. Activities are encoded as single symbols. labels.json : the mapping between activity labels and the symbols used in runs.txt . ambiguous.xes : the ambiguous event log, i.e. a set of traces in which events affected by ambiguity carry all their competing candidate activity labels. gold_standard.xes : the corresponding unambiguous log, used as ground truth for measuring disambiguation accuracy. Each log describes 15,000 executions of a process: Blood donation (BD): a blood-donation process synthesized from 32 real executions in an IoT-augmented lab setup. Smart home (SH): a smart-home process derived from the BP-Meets-IoT 2020 challenge dataset ( details ) by filtering for kitchen/eating-routine activities and discovering a model with the inductive miner. The sets of mutually ambiguous activities are {Check blood drawing machine, Take out samples} and {Disinfect injection site, Apply tourniquet, Insert needle, Remove tourniquet, Remove needle} for BD, and {Go fridge, Go dining table} , {Get cold warm food, Go kitchen shelf, Get food from fridge} , {Go micro, Get bread} for SH. The generated traces are stochastically perturbed to reflect IoT-based monitoring imperfections: process events are randomly skipped (simulating activities undetected by the IoT setup), and, for the healthcare scenario, additional hand hygiene events are inserted at random points (reflecting their unpredictable occurrence). Perturbation uses Java’s java.util.Random without a fixed seed, so each released log is one concrete instantiation of this stochastic process; the resulting traces may be non-conforming to the normative behavior. The third dataset used in the paper, HR recruitment (HR) , is a publicly available uncertain event log and is not redistributed here; it is available at its original repository (description: HaifaUniversityBPM/traffic-data-to-event-log ). Only its evaluation results are included (see below). results/ : the evaluation results for all three datasets ( X ∈ { BD , SH , HR }), one workbook per algorithm configuration: X_adaptive.xlsx : the adaptive algorithm (ABD in the paper). X_maxk_y.xlsx : the fixed-bound algorithm (FBD) with exploration bound maxK = y , for y = 1..5 . X_baseline.xlsx : the random-choice null-model baseline (RND), which has no access to the reference behavior and selects uniformly among the candidate labels of each ambiguous event. The random choice uses a fixed seed for reproducibility. Each workbook reports disambiguation quality and runtime for that configuration, organized into the following sheets: Summary : headline figures: dataset, algorithm (and maxK for FBD), number of events and traces, all-events disambiguation accuracy, mean fitness of the gold-standard and of the disambiguated traces, mean fitness drop, and mean runtime (per trace and per event). AllEvents : one row per event comparing the gold-standard label with the disambiguated label ( Are equal ); the basis of the all-events accuracy. Results : per-trace accuracy (total events, number of mismatches, accuracy). Fitness : per-case fitness of the gold-standard and disambiguated traces (run/trace length, synchronous and asynchronous moves, fitness) and the per-case fitness drop. Runtime_Ambiguous : per-trace runtime (ms) on the input log, with one column per measurement repeat and the average. The source code implementing the fixed-bound and adaptive algorithms is available in this GitHub repository .

items.summary: A phase-only spatial light modulator in the pupil of a microscope objective can form hundreds to thousands of optical traps at once, but only if the phase pattern it displays is computed well: the pattern fixes how much light reaches the traps, how equal the traps are, where stray light goes, how the pattern survives a real device, and how fast it can be recomputed when traps move. DinHot is an open studio that runs 24 methods (19 published ones and 5 proposed here) on the same task, with the same seeds, metrics and device model, in Python as the reference and in a TypeScript port that runs live in a browser. We describe the optical and device model, the methods with the measured acceptance of each, 14 cases from a 3 x 3 array to a disordered 819-trap array and shaped potentials, the benchmark protocol, two learned models, and the 5 proposed methods, three of which meet their acceptance criteria on their acceptance tasks, each within a scope that the benchmark or the scope measurements narrow (a device-aware weighted Gerchberg-Saxton update, a flicker-bounded phase-continuous sequence and an efficiency-uniformity front), one of which meets a narrowed criterion (an aberration-robust hologram) and one of which is refuted by measurement (a learned warm start for phase-fixed weighted GS). A network trained on three-plane volumes beats its baseline at equal wall-clock on all 162 held-out volumes (median accuracy ratio 1.140), whereas its two-dimensional counterpart ties with Gerchberg-Saxton (ratio 0.9994). The model is a scalar Fourier model of a simulated device, not a calibrated instrument. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . Interactive studio: https://dinhot.fasl-work.com .
